#513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id="1"]`, the contract this step's `command` names. Unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so command mode accepted contract #1 literally while interaction mode accepted whatever led the list -- two channels driving different contracts while both reported pass, because nothing asserted here can tell them apart (`activeContractCount` counts accepts, not identities). `level1-win-efficient` is what that costs once a `[data-contract-id]`-scoped assertion is added on top: its guard failed with its control absent from the DOM entirely, red on `main`, cause pointing nowhere near the accept step. ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-id` on offered cards (`makeOfferedCard`), so scoping removes the DOM-order coupling rather than baking around it.

BLOCKED, and deliberately not converted to a click: the ACTIVE card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled at this point. ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together whenever maxDeliverable = min(contract remaining, stored material) is 0, and a direct trace of this file shows 0.0 kg of blingite in storage against a 360 kg contract -- nothing in this scenario ever hauls material into storage. The console command is no better: it returns success:false and command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so `contract deliver 1 amount:800` is a silent no-op in BOTH modes today. `expect.blocked` is what now pins it down -- the button must be in the DOM and refused, with `expect.usable` on the panel's own storage link proving the panel is really open, so "blocked" cannot pass just because nothing is on screen. Forcing a click here would be asserting something the game correctly forbids.

expect.note: Findings #59-#60: `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` fails outright (tier-2, locked by default -- same class as Finding #58/the already-documented treranium_depths issue), so this file runs against the substitute new_game world throughout; not fixed here for the same reason. `employee assign_skill` used the same rejected positional syntax as Finding #45/#54 -- fixed to `skill:geology level:N`. All 5 of the `build` commands (`office`/`storage_depot`/`canteen`/`medical_bay`/`break_room`) name nonexistent building types, matching the established Finding #5/#47/#58 no-op pattern -- left unmarked rather than fixed, consistent with precedent. A `debris_hauler` is bought (along with a rock_digger and drill_rig); #552 makes hauling self-dispatching, so a driver no longer has to be assigned or a haul manually ordered for the fleet to try -- but this file's own 5 `build` commands all name nonexistent building types (the no-op pattern above), so no real freight_warehouse ever gets placed, `getStorageCapacity` stays 0, and every auto-created haul_debris PendingAction is claimable-but-never-completable for lack of anywhere to deliver to. Despite 4 real blasts, `storedMassKg` still stays 0 for the whole file and all 5 contract deliveries still fail honestly for lack of storage -- the same bottom line as before #552, now for a storage-capacity reason instead of a never-dispatched one; not fixed here either, since the hauling mechanism is already proven end-to-end by `level1-playthrough-win.json` and re-proving it here would cost the same again for no new verification value (Finding #59). Unusually for this batch, the file's own hardcoded contract IDs (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) all happened to match the real, currently-available pool at every listing -- no ID-mismatch fix was needed here, unlike every other multi-cycle-contract file this session. Finding #52's drill-grid class recurred a 4th time across all 4 of this file's grids (declared 12/16/20/20 holes vs. real 24/25/30/48) -- fixed the same way. The corrected, far larger grids are violent enough to kill 2 employees during the very first blast (deathCount 0→2, tick 32) -- a real, reproducible consequence, not a scenario bug. Discovered while investigating an unexplained $10,000-per-cycle income jump in `finances` output despite every delivery failing: some random events (at least `lucky_strike`) resolve silently and instantly inside a `tick` call -- the tick command's own output says 'No events fired' even as the event's transaction (`category:'contracts', description:'Event: lucky_strike'`) is added to the finance log -- a materially different mechanic from every other file's pending-choice events (`[tick N] EVENT: Name` + a required `event choose`). Because this file has real (if silent) events firing, `cash` is hard-asserted only through tick 32 (the first such event) and left unasserted after that, per Ground rule #12/Finding #34's established treatment, rather than assumed safe just because no `event choose` step was ever needed (Finding #60). No bankruptcy, revolt, or ecological shutdown within this file's 62-tick budget; safety and nuisance both bottom out at 0 from the accumulated real blast violence, matching the pattern from `level1-win-efficient.json`. ▸ 2026-08-08 (console funds guard, commit ddb88b3): the console now refuses a purchase the player cannot afford, so this file no longer reaches its state by overdrawing. The three vehicle buys used to overdraw to -$87,960 and stay there; the run is now funded with `new_game seed:2277 cash:150000` and they are `role: 'player'` clicks on enabled dealership rows, so cash never goes negative at all and ends at $32,530. Bankruptcy was never in play here before and still is not. Verified in both command mode and a real browser (interaction mode re-run twice for determinism, both clean), 108/108 steps.
